transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-07 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42 minutes | Attendees: Samir Patel, Maya Li - Redwood; Jordan Reyes, Priya Nair, Liam O'Connor - Polaris Tech

Summary: quick discovery focused on Redwood PLG quickstart, free credits and time-to-first-token for a small pilot. Customer is leaning hosted for initial experiment but has enterprise constraints (VPC, KMS) to evaluate dedicated/private for production. Next step is a benchmark pilot.

[00:00] Samir Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we really appreciate your time. Samir from Redwood, i'm the AE. with me is maya our solutions engineer, maya do you want to wave hi?
[00:07] Maya Li: hi all, maya li, SE on the account. we'll keep this pretty practical, demo the quickstart flow and talk about pilot options.
[00:13] Jordan Reyes: hi yeah jordan here, cto at polaris. thanks, we just want to understand how fast we can get up and running and what the path to dedicated or private looks like.
[00:23] Priya Nair: hey priya, lead ml eng. focused on latency targets and inference cost.
[00:28] Liam O'Connor: liam infra, i'll be evaluating networking and security stuff - VPC, peering, kms.

[01:00] Samir Patel: great, quick agenda: 1) quickstart / free credits / time-to-first-token, 2) what hosted gets you vs dedicated / private, 3) security and enterprise asks, 4) pilot next steps. does that align?
[01:12] Jordan Reyes: yep sounds good.

[02:00] Maya Li: so first, the quickstart: you can sign up, we give free credits for trial usage, and the goal is to get first tokens in under 10 minutes for most users using our SDKs. there are a few steps - API key, basic sample requests, and optional client-side streaming.
[02:22] Priya Nair: when you say free credits, is that account-scoped or per-team? and any throttles?
[02:28] Samir Patel: it's account-scoped; new accounts get credits for a 30 day window. throttles are conservative default limits but you can raise them; for pilot we usually bump limits.
[02:35] Priya Nair: okay. also, time-to-first-token, does that include model download time or is that only endpoint invocation?
[02:44] Maya Li: for hosted endpoints it's pure endpoint invocation. if you're self-hosting or using private on-prem there can be image / model load times on first warm-up; we mitigate with pre-warm and autoscaler policies.

[03:30] Liam O'Connor: what about SDKs and CI? would we be able to script onboarding as part of our infra pipelines?
[03:36] Maya Li: totally. we have rest and python sdks, examples for terraform/helm for private deploy, and a quickstart repo that you can fork. everything is scriptable.

[04:15] Jordan Reyes: for a pilot, our idea is to run a 2-week benchmark on a real workload, measure latency P95 and token cost. can redwood help tune batching and quantization?
[04:27] Samir Patel: yes, that's exactly what our optimize team and SEs do; maya will help with batching configs, kv cache settings, and we can recommend quantization profiles depending on output quality tolerance.

[05:00] Priya Nair: how do you preserve output quality with quantization? we worry about hallucinations rising if precision drops.
[05:08] Maya Li: good question. we run model-specific evals on your prompt set; we have rollback and A/B split rollouts, and we tie quality regressions to alerts. typical flow: try 4-bit quant, run evals, if quality is within threshold we keep it.

[06:00] Jordan Reyes: let's talk deployments. for the pilot we prefer hosted because faster, but for production we likely need VPC and KMS and audit logs. how heavy is the private deployment lift?
[06:12] Samir Patel: hosted is fastest - API keys, region selection, and you hit endpoints. dedicated is reserved capacity with dedicated GPU pools and SLA; private is customer-managed control plane with VPC and optionally on-prem. lift depends on networking and compliance: our private package includes setup for SAML/SSO, KMS integrations, and audit log ingestion.
[06:40] Liam O'Connor: does private support HSM or customer-managed KMS?
[06:44] Maya Li: yes, we support KMS integration and can integrate with HSM-backed providers for key wrapping. we'll share the security docs.

[07:30] Jordan Reyes: what about data retention and logs? we need audit trails and the ability to purge logs for GDPR.
[07:37] Samir Patel: we provide audit logs and configurable retention; for private deployments you control retention. hosted has retention settings and options for exporting logs to your S3.

[08:20] Priya Nair: can we run a small benchmark now or do we need a formal trial setup?
[08:25] Maya Li: we can do a lightweight benchmark using your sample payloads against our hosted endpoints using free credits. if you want guaranteed throughput or long-running tests we spin up a dedicated pilot cluster.

[09:00] Jordan Reyes: ok performance specifics: what's typical p95 for a 1k token generation on a 4096 context model on your hosted tier? just ballpark.
[09:09] Maya Li: ballpark, for a 7b-ish open architecture optimized model you might see 150-250ms per token at scale on our hosted fleet but it varies a lot with concurrency and batching. if you need tighter SLOs we recommend dedicated with optimized kernels and tuned batch sizes.

[10:00] Liam O'Connor: curious about caching - you mentioned KV cache earlier. how transparent is that to the developer?
[10:07] Maya Li: our runtime supports prefix/KV caching. you can opt-in; it caches intermediate KV states between similar requests to reduce compute. you get metrics in the console for cache hit rate. it's automatic for compatible models.

[11:00] Priya Nair: what's the fall-back if a hosted region is saturated? do you redirect to another model or degrade?
[11:07] Samir Patel: smart routing policy: we can route by latency, cost, region, or tier. we also support automatic fallback to compatible model variants or lower-cost quantized options to keep things online.

[12:00] Jordan Reyes: what about compliance docs - SOC2, ISO?
[12:05] Samir Patel: we are SOC 2 Type II. we'll send the pack after the call. for private deployments we do an expanded review and can support ISO needs via our compliance team.

[13:00] Priya Nair: okay, LLM-specific: do you support function/tool calling and structured outputs? our product uses function calls a lot.
[13:09] Maya Li: yes hosted API supports streaming, tool-calling and structured JSON outputs. we also have eval tooling to assert structure and content.

[14:00] Jordan Reyes: cost model: we want to understand per-token cost and reserved capacity pricing for dedicated - what's the commitment?
[14:08] Samir Patel: hosted is usage-based per-token. dedicated is reserved monthly or annual contracts with committed throughput. pricing depends on the GPU profile and committed throughput; we'll share a price sheet.

[15:00] Priya Nair: do you expose token-level billing per route in console?
[15:06] Maya Li: yep, per-route and per-model token breakdowns with cost and latency. you can set budgets and alerts.

[16:00] Liam O'Connor: regarding networking, do you support VPC peering or private link into our VPC?
[16:06] Samir Patel: for private deployments we do VPC and private connectivity; for hosted we support private endpoints and peering options in some regions. we'll share the network diagram.

[17:00] Jordan Reyes: how fast can we move from hosted pilot to dedicated? we want to avoid rewriting prompts if possible.
[17:08] Maya Li: the API is consistent, model versioning and rollout policies allow pinning model versions. moving to dedicated is mostly ops/provisioning time; we aim for non-breaking migrations.

[18:00] Priya Nair: curious about model catalog - do you host open models only or provide commercial models too?
[18:07] Samir Patel: catalog includes curated open models and Redwood-verified performance profiles; we also host certain commercial models via partner agreements.

[19:00] Jordan Reyes: any caveats about prompt latency when streaming?
[19:05] Maya Li: streaming reduces TTF and user perceived latency; network conditions matter though. we provide streaming SDKs with retries and partial results.

[20:00] Priya Nair: we have an internal requirement to run initial benchmarks with 100 concurrent users and a P95 under 500ms. feasible?
[20:08] Maya Li: feasible with dedicated and tuned batching; for hosted it depends on concurrent load on region and model. a short benchmark will tell us.

[21:00] Jordan Reyes: ok let's outline the pilot: 2-week hosted quickstart using free credits for functional validation, then a benchmark week where you help us measure P95 & token cost. if that looks good we'll discuss dedicated commitment.
[21:14] Samir Patel: sounds perfect. i'll send the quickstart steps and credits instructions. maya will handle the benchmark setup and run.

[22:00] Liam O'Connor: security ask: we need SSO integration and audit log exports to our SIEM, plus KMS for key wrapping.
[22:09] Maya Li: yep we support SAML SSO, RBAC roles, audit log exports to S3 or syslog, and KMS integrations. we'll attach the security pack.

[23:00] Priya Nair: any mention of SLA numbers for dedicated?
[23:05] Samir Patel: dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets - exact numbers vary by contract. we'll include SLA language in the follow-up.

[24:00] Jordan Reyes: okay can you do a short demo of quickstart flow in the console?
[24:06] Maya Li: sure i'll share my screen — sign-up, api key page, quickstart repo. copying commands: pip install redwood-sdk; export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...; python quickstart.py. it's typically under ten minutes to get first token.
[25:00] Maya Li: (demo) here is the console, here's model list, here's the quickstart sample request; note streaming toggle and function call examples. sometimes the transcriptions in docs call our products different names, i've seen KV cash typos in the wild, but it's KV cache.

[28:00] Jordan Reyes: hah yeah, we saw that in a slack thread. couple practical questions: can we pin a particular model version and get deterministic output across hosted and dedicated?
[28:10] Maya Li: yes you can pin model versions. deterministic output depends on sampling params but model versioning remains consistent.

[29:00] Priya Nair: what's the best way to measure quality regression when we move to quantized variants?
[29:07] Samir Patel: we recommend a set of prompts and metrics - we run automated evals and manual spot checks, tie regressions to alerts, and keep a rollback path.

[30:00] Liam O'Connor: about costs, do you have a calculator or a spreadsheet so we can estimate token spend?
[30:06] Samir Patel: yes we have a benchmark spreadsheet and unit economics calculator; i'll share it.

[31:00] Jordan Reyes: any concerns with us sharing sample prod-like data to run benchmarks? data is slightly sensitive but not PII.
[31:08] Maya Li: for hosted trial use obfuscated or synthetic samples if possible; for benchmark we can run in a private pilot or NDA. we'll coordinate.

[32:00] Priya Nair: timeline — we want pilot next week, then an internal review the week after.
[32:06] Samir Patel: great, we'll aim to start bench the week of 2026-05-11.

[33:00] Jordan Reyes: ok any competitors we should be aware of in our space? we've looked at anthrophic-ish vendors and openai.
[33:07] Samir Patel: yes folks often compare to anthology— sorry anthropic— and openai and cloud vendors. we try to compete on predictable inference economics and enterprise controls.

[34:00] Priya Nair: any docs or a checklist you can send for pilot onboarding?
[34:06] Maya Li: yes quickstart doc, security pack, benchmark spreadsheet, sample prompts template — i'll send them after call.

[35:00] Jordan Reyes: what are common pitfalls in pilot phase?
[35:06] Samir Patel: common ones are using unrealistic prompt sets, not accounting for cold-start model load times for private deployments, and not tuning batching. we'll help avoid them.

[36:00] Priya Nair: are there quotas on model variants we can try under free credits?
[36:05] Samir Patel: some premium partner models may be restricted but most open models and many verified models are available for trial.

[37:00] Maya Li: last note on migrations: our rollouts support A/B tests and canary deploys so you can validate variants against control.

[38:00] Jordan Reyes: OK let's recap next steps: samir send quickstart + credits + pricing; maya share benchmark spreadsheet, pilot run invite and security docs; jordan to send sample dataset.
[38:18] Samir Patel: yep i'll send that today.

[39:00] Priya Nair: thanks everyone, excited to try the quickstart.
[39:05] Liam O'Connor: thanks, i'll look for the network diagram and the security pack.
[39:10] Samir Patel: perfect, thanks all. we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark.

[40:00] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcript contains a few auto-transcription typos (e.g., KV cash instead of KV cache) and occasional speaker mislabels. The call followed a typical AE+SE discovery pattern with focus on quick time-to-first-token, pilot benchmarking, and enterprise security needs.
